finding: The real touch repeater lifecycle already tested Add/Delete and separate Save/Publish across six component types, but did not assert that focus returns to a surviving field after Delete, to the visible Add action after deleting the final row, or into the new row after Add.

coverage: On a 390x800 mobile, coarse-pointer Chromium context, touch Delete restores focus to the nearest surviving editable repeater field for list, tabs, accordion, dropdown, gallery and carousel.
Deleting the final repeater row returns focus to that type's visible Add button.
Touch Add puts focus inside the newly-created first row before authoring continues.
Existing assertions still prove repeater actions do not Save/Publish implicitly; explicit Save persists a draft, Editor reload restores it, and only separate Publish changes the public view.
change.test_stability: Raised the existing published mobile-tab state wait from 5 to 15 seconds after an unrelated slow-fixture timeout at 5 seconds; its state assertion remains strict.
